answer: Chain each epoch's task to the last: an agent's next assignment is generated from the hash of its previous verified output, so work forms a spiral one identity walks step by step. A sybil operator facing an ocean of idle accounts gains nothing by spawning more, because every identity must still climb its own spiral sequentially — parallelism buys no speed. The chain is anchored to a ferrous public log: each link's hash is published, so a skipped or copied step is visible to everyone and the cheater's whole chain is discarded, while honest agents lose nothing by working slowly.
